rules.fix_hint: In the setup code node, set default vars['outcome'] and vars['reason'] (e.g. not_reached/unconfirmed before verification, then no_promise/declined_offer after verification in prepare), so a call that ends by hang-up before any fin_* node still sends a valid enum outcome with a reason.

top_fixes.rule: If the customer says the full amount is too much, propose the floor once and say the remainder stays overdue and the account stays in arrears until cleared. Declining the floor is a flat refusal (rule 31). The floor may be named a second time only as attempt 2 (rule 31).
top_fixes.why: After the customer says the full amount is too much and the floor is offered, rung 0 'full_or_floor' can name the floor again outside attempt 2, so the floor is named an extra time and declining it isn't treated as a flat refusal. Too-much cases fail.
top_fixes.fix: Policy code `prepare`: set the rung-0 ladder entry to 'full' (or, when pg(V,pid,'offered_floor')=='yes', use 'full' instead of 'full_or_floor'). In `too_much()`, set `offered_floor='yes'` when `too_much_floor` is spoken, and send a decline of that floor offer to the flat-refusal path (rule 31). Name the floor again only in the attempt-2 rung.

top_fixes.rule: `close_call` is always the last tool call and nothing is accepted after it; `outcome` is one of the enum values; `reason` is required by the API for every outcome except `promise` and `paid` (the brief still assigns `full`/`partial` and `self_reported`).
top_fixes.why: If the customer hangs up before any fin_* node runs, `close_call` (end_of_call) sends an empty `{{outcome}}`/`{{reason}}`, which is an invalid enum value or a missing required reason, so the close_call check fails.
top_fixes.fix: Setup code node: add `vars['outcome']='not_verified'; vars['reason']='unconfirmed'` (or not_reached/unconfirmed, whichever the brief pairs for an early hang-up). In the post-verification `prepare` code, set `vars['outcome']='no_promise'; vars['reason']='declined_offer'`. The fin_* nodes then overwrite these defaults as they do now.

top_fixes.rule: Request for a person: do not ask whether you can help first; call `transfer_to_agent` queue `general` and close `transferred` / `agent_request`. Applies before and after the security check.
top_fixes.why: A request for a person made during the hardship flow goes to the care team instead of calling `transfer_to_agent` (queue general) and closing transferred/agent_request.
top_fixes.fix: Hardship node: add the value 'human' to its extraction enum (description: 'customer asks for a person/agent/human'). Add a first-priority transition `-> xfer_general if <field> equals "human"`, ahead of the care-team route, so it reaches fin_agent_request (transferred/agent_request) without asking whether the agent can help first.

top_fixes.rule: "This <weekday>" and "next <weekday>" both mean the first such weekday after today (said on a Wednesday, both "this Friday" and "next Friday" are the coming Friday).
top_fixes.why: 'This Friday' said on a Friday resolves to today instead of the following Friday, so the promise date is wrong.
top_fixes.fix: Policy code `resolve_when`, weekday branch: change `delta = (wd - today.weekday()) % 7` to `delta = (wd - today.weekday()) % 7 or 7` for both 'this' and 'next' (and a bare weekday) when weekday_rule == 'first_after'.
